table.name: alignment
table.purpose: Small lookup table mapping a numeric code (1-4) to a qualitative rating label (Good, Bad, Neutral, N/A). Referenced by t09, so it likely encodes a status/quality rating used there. With only 4 rows, the exact domain (e.g., customer satisfaction, credit rating, review score) cannot be determined from this table alone.

col_001.name: rating_code
col_001.description: Primary key of the lookup table; small integer code (1-4) identifying each rating. Referenced by t09.col_004 and t09.col_010, which store this code.

col_002.name: rating_label
col_002.description: Text label for the rating code: 'Good', 'Bad', 'Neutral', or 'N/A' (not applicable). The exact real-world meaning of the rating (what is being rated) is not determinable from this table alone.

table.name: attribute
table.purpose: A small lookup table of six power/ability rating categories (like a superhero power grid: Intelligence, Strength, Speed, Durability, Power, Combat). Other tables (t05, t09) reference these rows by id, presumably to store per-category ratings or scores. The exact domain (e.g. superheroes vs. game characters) cannot be confirmed from this table alone.

col_001.name: category_id
col_001.description: Primary key; surrogate integer id (1-6) for each rating category. Referenced by t05.col_002, t09.col_004 and t09.col_010.

col_002.name: category_name
col_002.description: Unique name of the rating category: Intelligence, Strength (implied by the six distinct values), Speed, Durability, Power, Combat.

table.purpose: A 35-row lookup table of colors (hair-like and general color names), each with a numeric id, referenced by other tables (t05, t09) as a foreign key. Likely a color/hair-color reference list; the exact domain (hair color vs. general color) is not fully determinable since values include both natural hair colors (Blond, Auburn, Strawberry Blond) and general colors (Magenta, Silver, Gold).

col_001.name: color_id
col_001.description: Primary key; surrogate integer identifier (1-35) for each color entry. Referenced as a foreign key by t05.col_002 and several columns of t09.

col_002.name: color_name
col_002.description: Unique name of the color, e.g. Black, Blond, Magenta, Silver, Strawberry Blond. Mix of natural hair-color terms and general color terms, so the precise domain (hair color list vs. general color list) is ambiguous.

table.name: gender_lookup
table.purpose: Small lookup table mapping a numeric gender code to a gender label (Male, Female, N/A). Likely referenced by other tables via col_001, though no explicit joins were detected in this snapshot (only 3 rows).

col_001.name: gender_code
col_001.description: Numeric primary key / code for the gender category (1 = Male, 2 = Female, 3 = N/A).

table.name: hero_attribute_scores
table.purpose: Long-format table of superhero attribute ratings: one row per hero per attribute, with a numeric score from 5 to 100. 623 heroes x 6 attributes = 3738 rows. The attribute lookup (t02) labels values 1-6 as Intelligence, Speed, Durability, Power, Combat (and by elimination, 2 = Strength).

col_001.name: hero_id
col_001.description: Identifier of the hero being rated; references t09.col_001 (many-to-one). 623 distinct heroes, each appearing 6 times (once per attribute).

col_002.name: attribute_id
col_002.description: Attribute being scored, 1-6, referencing lookup t02 (Intelligence, Speed, Durability, Power, Combat; value 2 is most likely Strength, the one label not shown in the sample pairs). Joins to t03/t07 are spurious statistical coincidences, not real references.

col_003.name: score
col_003.description: Rating for the hero on that attribute, on a 5-100 scale (min 5, max 100, median 50). Joins to t09/t10 are coincidental integer matches, not real references.

table.purpose: t06 appears to be a junction/association table linking two entities: one identified by col_001 (referencing t09) and one identified by col_002 (referencing t10). Each row represents a relationship between a member of t09 and a member of t10. The exact business meaning (e.g., assignment, enrollment, membership) cannot be determined from the data alone, since all values are opaque integer identifiers with no labels or lookup pairs available. The fact that col_002 also joins t09.col_001 statistically may indicate t09 and t10 share an identifier domain, or that the join is spurious; this is unresolved. The table has no single-column primary key detected, consistent with a composite-key link table, though no composite key analysis was provided to confirm this.

col_001.name: t09_reference_id
col_001.description: Integer identifier referencing a row in table t09 (many-to-one). Values range 1-756 with 652 distinct values, each appearing a handful of times (max 49 occurrences), consistent with a foreign key into a ~652-row parent table. The specific entity it identifies (e.g., a person, product, or account) is unknown because t09's contents were not provided.

col_002.name: t10_reference_id
col_002.description: Integer identifier referencing a row in table t10 (many-to-one). Values range 1-167 with 167 distinct values, each appearing many times (up to 358), consistent with a foreign key into a ~167-row parent table. It also statistically joins t09.col_001; this may mean t09 and t10 share an identifier space, or that the t09 join is coincidental. The underlying entity is unresolved.

table.name: franchise_owner
table.purpose: Lookup table of franchises/creators (media and entertainment properties and their owners/creators), each with a unique name; referenced by other tables (t05, t09).

col_001.name: franchise_id
col_001.description: Primary key; sequential integer identifier 1-25 for each franchise/creator entry.

col_002.name: franchise_name
col_002.description: Unique name of the franchise, creator, or rights holder (e.g. 'DC Comics', 'J. K. Rowling', 'Sony Pictures', 'Shueisha'). One row has an empty string, so one entry is unnamed in the data.

table.name: race
table.purpose: A lookup table of character species/race categories (e.g., Alien, Mutant, Vampire, Android, Demi-God, Inhuman, Spartoi), one row per species. Referenced by t09, which appears to be a character table linking each character to a species via several columns (col_005 through col_009). The 61 rows suggest a fixed enumeration of races, including '-' for unspecified/none.

col_001.name: species_id
col_001.description: Primary key; sequential integer identifier (1-61) for each species/race entry. Referenced by t09 columns col_005-col_009, which appear to be species-related foreign keys on a character table.

col_002.name: species_name
col_002.description: Unique name of the species/race (e.g., Alien, Alpha, Amazon, Android, Mutant, Demi-God, Vampire, Symbiote, Inhuman, Spartoi, 'Human / Radiation'). '-' likely denotes unspecified/none.

table.name: superhero
table.purpose: One row per fictional character (superhero/villain) with name, identity, alignment, physical attributes and stat/publisher references. Matches the classic 'SuperheroDB' dataset.

col_001.name: character_id
col_001.description: Primary key, unique integer identifier for each character (1-756).

col_002.name: superhero_name
col_002.description: Character's alias/hero name, e.g. 'Green Lantern V', 'Iceman', 'King Kong'.

col_003.name: full_name
col_003.description: Character's real/full name, e.g. 'Barbara Gordon', 'Jessica Viviana Cruz'. '-' or null when unknown.

col_005.name: eye_color_id
col_005.description: References t03 colour lookup (Black, Magenta, Pink, Violet, White...). Most plausible reading is eye colour, but the same lookup also fits hair/skin colour; which of col_005/col_006/col_007 maps to which colour attribute is not determinable from the evidence alone.

col_006.name: hair_color_id
col_006.description: References t03 colour lookup. Plausibly hair colour (26 distinct values, wider spread than col_005), but could be another colour attribute; exact assignment unresolved.

col_007.name: skin_color_id
col_007.description: References t03 colour lookup; heavily skewed to value 1 (681/750), consistent with a default/normal skin colour. Could equally be another colour attribute; exact assignment unresolved.

col_008.name: race_id
col_008.description: References t08 race lookup (e.g. Human / Radiation, Inhuman, Spartoi, Talokite, Zombie). Dominant values 1 and 24 likely 'Human' variants.

col_009.name: publisher_id
col_009.description: References t07 publisher lookup (e.g. DC Comics, Microsoft, Shueisha, Team Epic TV, Titan Books). Top values 13 and 4 correspond to major comics publishers.

col_010.name: alignment_duplicate
col_010.description: Same 1/2/3 coding and distribution as col_004, referencing the t01 Good/Bad/Neutral lookup; appears to be a duplicate alignment column.

col_011.name: height_cm
col_011.description: Character height in centimetres: median 178, p25-p75 ~159-188, typical human range; 0 and extreme outliers (e.g. 10800, 30480) present. Null when unknown.

col_012.name: weight_kg
col_012.description: Character weight in kilograms: median 72, typical human range, with 0 and extreme outliers (up to 90,000,000) for non-human characters. Null when unknown.

table.name: superhero_powers
table.purpose: Lookup table of superpowers/abilities, one row per distinct power. Referenced by other tables (e.g. t09) that assign powers to characters or heroes.

col_001.name: power_id
col_001.description: Primary key; surrogate integer identifier for a power (1-167, sequential).

col_002.name: power_name
col_002.description: Unique human-readable name of the superpower/ability (e.g. 'Invisibility', 'Accelerated Healing', 'Power Nullifier').
